D012-D018_h001.question:
I’ve always been someone who keeps things together—my team at the bank relies on me, and at home, my husband says I’m the steady one. But for about six months now, I’ve been struggling in ways I can’t explain. If I see blood—even a small cut, or someone getting a shot at the pharmacy—it hits me like a switch. My heart slams, I can’t breathe, I sweat out of nowhere, and sometimes I feel like I’m going to pass out. It’s gotten so I avoid anything medical. I skipped my physical this year and I white-knuckle it during flu season.

It’s funny—this never used to bother me. Maybe it started around the time of… well, an incident last year. I was in the parking garage after work when something happened—nothing violent, just scary. I’d rather not say more. But since then, I notice I’m more jumpy, and my body seems to react to things faster, like it’s on high alert sometimes. But I don’t have nightmares or constantly think about it—I’m not *that* out of control. Still, when it comes to blood or needles, my body just… overreacts.
D012-D018_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D012-D018_h001.answer: D & A. Specific Phobia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h002.question: I’ve been having these intense waves of panic whenever I have to drive the bus through the city tunnel—it started maybe four months ago, though I can’t pinpoint why. The moment I see the entrance, my chest tightens, my heart slams like it’s trying to get out, and I feel like I can’t breathe. It’s not just stress; it’s like something inside me screams to stop, to turn back. Sometimes I’ve even asked another driver to take my route, which is embarrassing at my age, especially since I’ve been doing this job for over twenty years. My wife says I’ve been jumpy, waking up mid-dream like I’m fighting something, but I don’t remember much. There was an incident a few years back—on the job—something with an accident I’d rather not talk about. I didn’t need counseling then, but now… I don’t know if this fear is leftover from that, or just something new. I don’t avoid other tight spaces, like the garage or restrooms, just that tunnel. It doesn’t happen every time I face it, but when it does, it’s overwhelming—like the walls are closing in. I can’t tell if this is just a bad reaction or something deeper.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h003.question:
I’ve been having these waves of fear that come out of nowhere—well, not *nowhere*. They always seem to follow certain things, like loud noises or when someone gets too animated, almost like a switch flips. There was this one time at work, a kid dropped a stack of coins and the clatter was so sharp, I just… froze. Couldn’t move, couldn’t speak—felt like my body shut down for what felt like minutes, even though people said it was only seconds. It’s happened a few times since then, mostly around sudden sounds or when people wear hats that shadow their faces, like mascots at events. I know it sounds strange, but it brings back this thick, heavy feeling, like something awful is about to happen.  

I don’t like talking about it, because I can’t really explain why it hits me so hard. There *was* something a few years back—around the time of my divorce—but I don’t want to make too much of it. I just know that now, I avoid crowds, the mall during holidays with all those costumed characters… even the break room if people are laughing too loud. I can still do my job, but I’m always watching, waiting for the next sound, the next moment I won’t be able to control.

    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h004.question:

It hits me the second the door closes, like I can’t breathe, my heart’s pounding, and I just need to get out. It didn’t used to be like this.     D. Specific Phobia

    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h006.question:

D012-D018_h009.question:
